chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed that a slave be freed for him with five hundred dirhams from his third. So a slave was bought for less than five hundred dirhams, and a remainder remained. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The remainder should be given to the slave before he is freed, then he is freed on behalf of the deceased.'
ai.seo_question: What happens to the leftover money when buying a slave for emancipation costs less than the bequeathed amount?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distribution of surplus funds from the bequeathed third (thuluth) used for manumitting a slave. The ruling dictates that the excess amount is transferred to the slave before their official emancipation, effectively increasing their capital or value while they are still in bondage, ensuring the beneficiary receives the full intended benefit of the bequest. This highlights the Shia juristic principle of maximizing the utility of bequeathed assets for the specific purpose designated by the deceased.
